metadata.title: How to Audit a Reference List
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week09/term2-week9-video-content.md (Week 9); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: STEM/learning film, hai Plain register on the ai-explainer chassis. Thesis: audit a reference list in four steps — does it exist (exact title in Scholar/Crossref/arXiv, a named venue in its own proceedings), do the details match, add a DOI, does it support the claim — and trust only the record itself. Worked example: our 24 references, 2 fabricated and 7 with wrong details. On-screen data numbers appear in the Week 9 source; the Your Turn size (five) is Janvi's supplied task.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about auditing a reference list, especially one drafted with AI help. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: An AI tool helped me draft my reference list. How do I check that every citation is real and correct?
props.segment: How to Audit a Reference List.
output: Match every detail and add a DOI

beats.role_note: A citation that looks perfect (our [14], Elkins & Kochmar, BEA 2023) with a 'does it exist?' stamp; chip 'ours: 2 of 24 fabricated, 7 wrong details'.
beats.narration_text: AI writing tools can produce citations that look perfect and don't exist. In our 24 references, two were fabricated, and seven had wrong details.
beats.visual_intent: A citation that looks perfect (our [14], Elkins & Kochmar, BEA 2023) with a 'does it exist?' stamp; chip 'ours: 2 of 24 fabricated, 7 wrong details'.

beats.role_note: Step 1 card 'Does it exist?': exact title → Google Scholar · Crossref · arXiv; named venue → its own proceedings.
beats.narration_text: Step one: does it exist? Search the exact title in Google Scholar, Crossref or arXiv. If a venue is named, search that venue's own proceedings.
beats.visual_intent: Step 1 card 'Does it exist?': exact title → Google Scholar · Crossref · arXiv; named venue → its own proceedings.

beats.role_note: Step 2 card 'Do the details match?': authors and initials · title · venue · year · pages; examples: wrong authors · preprint listed as conference · wrong pages.
beats.narration_text: Step two: do the details match? Check every author name and initial, the title, the venue, the year and the page numbers. Our errors hid there: wrong authors, a preprint listed as a conference paper, and wrong pages.
beats.visual_intent: Step 2 card 'Do the details match?': authors and initials · title · venue · year · pages; examples: wrong authors · preprint listed as conference · wrong pages.

show.event: authors and initials · title · venue · year · pages
our errors: wrong authors · preprint as conference · wrong pages

beats.role_note: Step 3 card 'Add a DOI' (example DOI from our replacement [6]); chip 'no DOI found → look harder'.
beats.narration_text: Step three: add a DOI. If you can't find one, that's a signal to look harder.
beats.visual_intent: Step 3 card 'Add a DOI' (example DOI from our replacement [6]); chip 'no DOI found → look harder'.

beats.role_note: Step 4 card 'Does it support the claim?': your sentence ↔ the paper; 'replaced a citation → re-read its sentence'.
beats.narration_text: Step four: check the claim. Read enough of the paper to confirm it says what your sentence says it does. When you replace a citation, re-read the sentence it supports.
beats.visual_intent: Step 4 card 'Does it support the claim?': your sentence ↔ the paper; 'replaced a citation → re-read its sentence'.

show.event: replaced a citation → re-read its sentence

beats.role_note: When NOT to trust: 'sounds right' · 'an AI tool says it exists' · 'similar title in search' all struck; 'the record itself' kept.
beats.narration_text: What not to trust: a citation that sounds right, an AI tool's confirmation that it exists, or a search result with a similar title. Only the record itself counts.
beats.visual_intent: When NOT to trust: 'sounds right' · 'an AI tool says it exists' · 'similar title in search' all struck; 'the record itself' kept.

show.event: an AI tool says it exists ✗

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick five references from your latest draft and run all four steps. Count how many pass every one.

props.command: Here are five references. For each: exists? details match? DOI? supports my sentence?
